title: Weekend plans with Sēf
goal: Say what you'll do on Saturday and accept Sēf's invitation to the desert
tip: For the future, put b- on the present verb: arūḥ → barūḥ 'I'll go', tsawwi → bitsawwi 'you'll do', akūn → bakūn 'I'll be', ayīb → bayīb 'I'll bring'. You know barūḥ already. When a time word shows the future, the b- can drop: bāchir arūḥ.
grammar: future b-: I and you (barūḥ, bitsawwi)
dialogue: A
سالم، شو بتسوي يوم السبت؟
Sālim, shu bitsawwi yōm is-sabt?
Salim, what are you doing on Saturday?
B
ما أدري. يمكن بنام طول اليوم! وانت؟
ma adri. yimkin banām ṭūl il-yōm! w inta?
I don't know. Maybe I'll sleep all day! And you?
A
أنا بروح البر ويا الشباب. بتيي؟
ana barūḥ il-barr wiyya sh-shabāb. bitiyi?
I'm going to the desert with the guys. Are you coming?
B
أكيد! بتمر علي؟
akīd! bitmurr ʿalay?
Definitely! Will you pick me up?
A
هيه، بمر عليك الساعة أربع
hē, bamurr ʿalēk is-sāʿa arbaʿ
Yes, I'll pick you up at four.
B
زين، بكون جاهز. وبييب الماي
zēn, bakūn jāhiz. w bayīb il-māy
Great, I'll be ready. And I'll bring the water.
A
حلو! وبيكون الجو حلو في البر
ḥilu! w biykūn il-jaww ḥilu fi l-barr
Nice! And the weather will be lovely in the desert.
items: what are you going to do? what are you doing (later)? (to a man)
to a woman: shu bitsawwīn? (شو بتسوين)
will you come? are you coming? (to a man)
to a woman: bitiyīn? (بتيين); you'll see written بتجي
will you pick me up? will you come by for me? (to a man)
I'll pick you up, I'll come by for you (to a man)
to a woman: bamurr ʿalēch (بمر عليج)
she'll be, you'll be: bitkūn (بتكون); il-jaww = the weather
culture: In the cooler months, roughly November to March, many people in the UAE drive out to the desert (il-barr) at the weekend with friends or family: they sit on rugs round a fire, grill food, drink tea and chat late into the night. In summer it is far too hot for this.

title: Turning down a dinner
goal: Tell Maryam you can't come to the office dinner, and promise you won't forget tomorrow's meeting
tip: To say you won't do something, put ma before the b- verb: ma barūḥ 'I won't go', ma bagdar 'I won't be able to', ma bansa 'I won't forget', ma batʼakhkhar 'I won't be late'. You'll also hear ma rāḥ arūḥ, which is more Kuwaiti.
dialogue: A
سالم، عندنا عشا يوم الخميس، كل المكتب. بتيي؟
Sālim, ʿindana ʿasha yōm il-khamīs, kill il-maktab. bitiyi?
Salim, we're having a dinner on Thursday, the whole office. Are you coming?
B
آسف، ما بقدر. عندي امتحان يوم الجمعة
āsif, ma bagdar. ʿindi imtiḥān yōm il-jumʿa
Sorry, I can't make it. I've got an exam on Friday.
A
خسارة! وبعد الامتحان؟ بنروح السينما
khasāra! w baʿd il-imtiḥān? binrūḥ is-sīnama
What a shame! And after the exam? We're going to the cinema.
B
لا والله، ما بروح. برجع البيت وبنام!
la wallāh, ma barūḥ. barjaʿ il-bēt w banām!
No, honestly, I'm not going. I'll go home and sleep!
A
زين. بس باكر عندنا اجتماع الساعة ثمان. لا تنسى!
zēn. bas bāchir ʿindana ijtimāʿ is-sāʿa thamān. la tinsa!
OK. But tomorrow we've got a meeting at eight. Don't forget!
B
لا تحاتين، ما بنسى وما بتأخر
la tḥātīn, ma bansa w ma batʼakhkhar
Don't worry, I won't forget and I won't be late.
A
زين! والمرة الياية بتيي ويانا
zēn! w il-marra l-yāya bitiyi wiyyāna
Good! And next time you're coming with us.
items: I won't be able to, I can't make it
I won't go, I'm not going
Kuwait-leaning: ma rāḥ arūḥ (ما راح أروح)
you'll see written المرة الجاية; same as il-marra th-thānya (المرة الثانية)

title: Who's going? The desert trip
goal: Plan the desert trip with Sēf: say what we'll do there and what the others will do
tip: b- goes on every person: nrūḥ → binrūḥ 'we'll go', yrūḥ → biyrūḥ 'he'll go', trūḥ → bitrūḥ 'she'll go', yrūḥūn → biyrūḥūn 'they'll go'. biyṣīr means 'it'll happen, it'll get': biyṣīr il-jaww bārid 'it'll get cold'. The b- can drop on a second verb: binsōlif w nishrab chāy.
grammar: future b-: we, he, she, they (binrūḥ, biyrūḥūn)
dialogue: B
سيف، متى بنروح يوم السبت؟
Sēf, mita binrūḥ yōm is-sabt?
Sēf, when are we going on Saturday?
A
بنروح بعد العصر. الشباب بيروحون قبلنا
binrūḥ baʿd il-ʿaṣir. ish-shabāb biyrūḥūn gabilna
We'll go after the afternoon prayer. The guys will go before us.
B
زين. وشو بنسوي هناك؟
zēn. w shu binsawwi hnāk?
OK. And what will we do there?
A
بنسولف ونشرب شاي. وبيصير الجو بارد في الليل
binsōlif w nishrab chāy. w biyṣīr il-jaww bārid fi l-lēl
We'll chat and drink tea. And it'll get cold at night.
B
والله؟ زين، بلبس جاكيت
wallāh? zēn, balbas jākēt
Really? OK, I'll wear a jacket.
A
وأمي بتسوي لنا عيش ودياي
w ummi bitsawwī-lna ʿēsh w diyāy
And my mum will make us rice and chicken.
B
ما شاء الله! بيكون يوم حلو
mā shāʼ allāh! biykūn yōm ḥilu
Wow! It's going to be a great day.
items: he'll go: biyrūḥ; she'll go: bitrūḥ
ysōlif = to chat; UAE also: yirmis (يرمس) 'to talk'
it'll happen; it'll get, it'll turn
biyṣīr il-jaww bārid = it'll get cold
you'll make us, said to a man, sounds the same

title: A promise to Maryam
goal: Ask Maryam about her day in Sharjah and promise to finish the file while she's out
tip: Talking to a woman, the future keeps -īn: bitrūḥīn 'you'll go', bitsawwīn 'you'll do', bitiyīn 'you'll come'. To promise, use b- with the verb: bakhallṣah 'I'll finish it', bakhabbrich 'I'll let you know'. waʿd? 'promise?' gets the answer waʿd! 'I promise!'
grammar: future b- to a woman: bitrūḥīn, bitsawwīn
dialogue: B
مريم، بتروحين الشارقة باكر؟
Maryam, bitrūḥīn ish-Shārja bāchir?
Maryam, are you going to Sharjah tomorrow?
A
هيه، عندي اجتماع هناك. بطلع من البيت الساعة سبع
hē, ʿindi ijtimāʿ hnāk. baṭlaʿ min il-bēt is-sāʿa sabʿ
Yes, I've got a meeting there. I'll leave home at seven.
B
زين. وشو بتسوين بعد الاجتماع؟
zēn. w shu bitsawwīn baʿd il-ijtimāʿ?
OK. And what will you do after the meeting?
A
برجع المكتب. بس الملف لازم يخلص الصبح!
barjaʿ il-maktab. bas il-malaff lāzim yikhlaṣ iṣ-ṣubḥ!
I'll come back to the office. But the file has to be done in the morning!
B
لا تحاتين، أنا بخلصه وبخبرج
la tḥātīn, ana bakhallṣah w bakhabbrich
Don't worry, I'll finish it and let you know.
A
وعد؟
waʿd?
Promise?
B
وعد! وانتي متى بتيين المكتب؟
waʿd! w inti mita bitiyīn il-maktab?
I promise! And when will you come into the office?
items: you'll go, are you going? (to a woman)
baṭlaʿ min il-bēt = I'll leave home
what are you going to do? (to a woman)
it has to be finished, it must be done
yikhlaṣ = it ends, it's done; don't confuse with ykhalliṣ 'he finishes (something)'
I'll let you know, I'll tell you (to a woman)
will you come? are you coming? (to a woman)
to a man: bitiyi?; you'll see written بتجين

title: Checkpoint 2.1: a study day with the guys
goal: Plan a library day with Sēf and his classmates: ask the group about tomorrow, offer coffee and promise to be on time
tip: Talking to a group, present and future verbs end in -ūn: tsawwūn → bitsawwūn 'you'll do', la tḥātūn 'don't worry'. 'We' takes n-: binmurr 'we'll come by', ma binitrayyāk 'we won't wait for you'. 'With you all' is wiyyākum, 'for you all' -lkum.
dialogue: B
هلا شباب! شو بتسوون باكر؟
hala shabāb! shu bitsawwūn bāchir?
Hi guys! What are you doing tomorrow?
A
هلا فيك! بنروح المكتبة وندرس طول اليوم. بتيي؟
hala fīk! binrūḥ il-maktaba w nidris ṭūl il-yōm. bitiyi?
Hi! We're going to the library to study all day. Are you coming?
B
أكيد! بس سيارتي مب زينة. أروح وياكم؟
akīd! bas sayyārti mub zēna. arūḥ wiyyākum?
Definitely! But my car's playing up. Can I go with you?
A
هيه، بنمر عليك الساعة تسع
hē, binmurr ʿalēk is-sāʿa tisʿ
Yes, we'll pick you up at nine.
B
زين! وبييب لكم قهوة
zēn! w bayīb-lkum gahwa
Great! And I'll bring you all coffee.
A
حلو! بس لا تتأخر، ما بنترياك!
ḥilu! bas la titʼakhkhar, ma binitrayyāk!
Nice! But don't be late, we won't wait for you!
B
لا تحاتون، بكون جاهز قبلكم!
la tḥātūn, bakūn jāhiz gabilkum!
Don't worry, I'll be ready before you!
items: what are you going to do? (to a group)
to one man: shu bitsawwi?; to one woman: shu bitsawwīn?
to one man: wiyyāk; to one woman: wiyyāch; with us: wiyyāna
we'll pick you up, we'll come by for you (to a man)
to one man: bayīb-lak; to one woman: bayīb-lich
we won't wait for you (to a man)
to one man: la tḥāti; to one woman: la tḥātīn

title: What are you up to? A call from Sēf
goal: Answer Sēf's call, say what you're doing right now and end the call when someone else rings
tip: For 'doing right now', put gāʿid before the present verb: gāʿid adhākir 'I'm revising', gāʿid tsūg? 'are you driving?', gāʿid ashrab 'I'm drinking'. On its own gāʿid means 'sitting'. It agrees with the person: a woman says gāʿda (next lesson).
dialogue: A
ألو، هلا سالم! شو قاعد تسوي؟
alō, hala Sālim! shu gāʿid tsawwi?
Hello, hi Salim! What are you up to?
B
هلا فيك! قاعد أذاكر حق الامتحان
hala fīk! gāʿid adhākir ḥagg il-imtiḥān
Hi! I'm revising for the exam.
A
الحين؟ يا ريّال، الساعة عشر!
il-ḥīn? yā rayyāl, is-sāʿa ʿashr!
Now? Man, it's ten o'clock!
B
هيه، الامتحان باكر. وانت؟ قاعد تسوق؟
hē, il-imtiḥān bāchir. w inta? gāʿid tsūg?
Yes, the exam's tomorrow. And you? Are you driving?
A
لا، قاعد أشرب كرك ويا الشباب. تبي تيي؟
la, gāʿid ashrab karak wiyya sh-shabāb. tabi tiyi?
No, I'm having a karak with the guys. Do you want to come?
B
ما أقدر، قاعد أذاكر! لحظة، أحد يتصل. بكلمك بعدين
ma agdar, gāʿid adhākir! laḥẓa, aḥad yittaṣil. bakallmak baʿdēn
I can't, I'm revising! Hang on, someone's calling. I'll call you later.
A
زين، يلا باي!
zēn, yalla bāy!
OK, bye then!
items: what are you doing (right now)? (to a man)
to a woman: shu gāʿda tsawwīn?
am / is …-ing, in the middle of (a man; before a present verb)
a woman: gāʿda; a group: gāʿdīn; UAE also: yālis (يالس); alone it means 'sitting'
I'm revising, I'm studying (for an exam) (said by a man)
ḥagg = for: ḥagg il-mudīr = for the manager
I'll call you later, I'll talk to you later (to a man)

title: Calling Maryam in the car
goal: Call Maryam, find out what she's doing and ask her one quick question about the meeting
tip: With a woman, gāʿid becomes gāʿda and the 'you' verb keeps -īn: shu gāʿda tsawwīn? 'what are you doing?', gāʿda tsūgīn? 'are you driving?'. A woman about herself: gāʿda asūg 'I'm driving'. About a man: il-mudīr gāʿid yitrayyāk 'the manager is waiting for you'.
grammar: progressive to and about a woman: gāʿda + -īn
dialogue: B
ألو مريم، شحالج؟ عندج وقت؟
alō Maryam, shḥālich? ʿindich wagt?
Hello Maryam, how are you? Have you got a moment?
A
بخير الله يسلمك. هيه، تفضل
b-khēr, allāh ysallmak. hē, tfaẓẓal
Fine, thank you. Yes, go ahead.
B
شو قاعدة تسوين؟ انتي في السيارة؟
shu gāʿda tsawwīn? inti fi s-sayyāra?
What are you doing? Are you in the car?
A
هيه، قاعدة أسوق، رايحة المكتب
hē, gāʿda asūg, rāyḥa l-maktab
Yes, I'm driving, on my way to the office.
B
زين، سؤال واحد بس: الاجتماع الساعة كم؟
zēn, suʼāl wāḥid bas: il-ijtimāʿ is-sāʿa cham?
OK, just one question: what time's the meeting?
A
الساعة عشر. والمدير قاعد يترياك!
is-sāʿa ʿashr. w il-mudīr gāʿid yitrayyāk!
At ten. And the manager's waiting for you!
B
أنا ياي! وانتي لا تسوقين بسرعة
ana yāy! w inti la tsūgīn b-surʿa
I'm on my way! And don't drive too fast.
items: am / is …-ing (a woman; before a present verb)
a man: gāʿid; alone it means 'sitting' (a woman)
what are you doing (right now)? (to a woman)
to a man: shu gāʿid tsawwi?
have you got a moment? are you free? (to a woman)
suʼāl wāḥid bas = just one question
he's waiting for you (to a man)
to a woman: yitrayyāch; Kuwait: yinṭrak (ينطرك)
to a man: la tsūg b-surʿa

title: Watching the match at Sēf's
goal: Call Sēf and his friends, find out what they're all doing and say you'll join them
tip: For we, they or a group, gāʿid becomes gāʿdīn: gāʿdīn nshūf 'we're watching', shu gāʿdīn tsawwūn? 'what are you all doing?'. For one person it stays gāʿid or gāʿda: minu gāʿid yilʿab? 'who's playing?', ummi gāʿda tsawwi ʿasha 'my mum's making dinner'.
grammar: progressive with we, they and a group: gāʿdīn
dialogue: B
ألو سيف! انتو وين؟ شو قاعدين تسوون؟
alō Sēf! intu wēn? shu gāʿdīn tsawwūn?
Hello Sēf! Where are you guys? What are you all doing?
A
نحن في البيت، قاعدين نشوف المباراة
niḥin fi l-bēt, gāʿdīn nshūf il-mubārā
We're at home, watching the match.
B
زين! منو قاعد يلعب؟
zēn! minu gāʿid yilʿab?
Nice! Who's playing?
A
الإمارات! تعال، الشباب كلهم هني
il-Imārāt! taʿāl, ish-shabāb killhum hni
The UAE! Come over, all the guys are here.
B
زين، ياي الحين. تبون شي؟
zēn, yāy il-ḥīn. tabūn shay?
OK, coming now. Do you want anything?
A
لا، أمي قاعدة تسوي لنا عشا
la, ummi gāʿda tsawwī-lna ʿasha
No, my mum's making us dinner.
B
حلو! يلا، عشر دقايق وأنا عندكم
ḥilu! yalla, ʿashr dagāyig w ana ʿindakum
Great! OK, I'll be with you in ten minutes.
items: are …-ing (we, they, a group; before a present verb)
one man: gāʿid; one woman: gāʿda; alone it means 'sitting'
what are you doing (right now)? (to a group)
to one man: shu gāʿid tsawwi?; to one woman: shu gāʿda tsawwīn?
at your place, with you (a group); you have (a group)
to one man: ʿindak; to one woman: ʿindich
culture: Big football matches, above all the national team's, are often watched together: friends gather at someone's house or majlis, the family brings food and tea, and the room reacts loudly to every chance. Going over to join is normal; you don't need a formal invitation from a close friend.

title: A bad line on the metro
goal: Deal with a bad line on the metro: check Sēf can hear you, call him back, and say Maryam isn't answering
tip: To say something isn't happening right now, put mub before gāʿid: mub gāʿid asmaʿak 'I can't hear you (right now)', Maryam mub gāʿda trudd 'Maryam isn't answering'. Kuwaitis say mū gāʿid. For a woman: mub gāʿda.
dialogue: A
ألو؟ سالم؟
alō? Sālim?
Hello? Salim?
B
هلا سيف! تسمعني؟ أنا في المترو
hala Sēf! tismaʿni? ana fi l-mitrō
Hi Sēf! Can you hear me? I'm on the metro.
A
الصوت مب واضح. مب قاعد أسمعك زين
iṣ-ṣōt mub wāẓiḥ. mub gāʿid asmaʿak zēn
The sound isn't clear. I can't hear you properly.
B
زين، بتصل فيك بعد دقيقة
zēn, battaṣil fīk baʿd dagīga
OK, I'll call you back in a minute.
A
هلا! الحين أسمعك. الشبكة في المترو مب زينة
hala! il-ḥīn asmaʿak. ish-shabaka fi l-mitrō mub zēna
Hi! I can hear you now. The signal on the metro is bad.
B
اتصلت في مريم، بس مب قاعدة ترد
ittaṣalt fi Maryam, bas mub gāʿda trudd
I called Maryam, but she isn't answering.
A
يمكن الشبكة عندها مب زينة بعد. بكلمها أنا بعدين
yimkin ish-shabaka ʿind-ha mub zēna baʿad. bakallimha ana baʿdēn
Maybe her signal's bad too. I'll call her later.
items: can you hear me? (to a man)
I can't hear you (right now) (said by a man, to a man)
a woman says: mub gāʿda asmaʿak; to a woman: asmaʿich; Kuwait: mū gāʿid
to a woman: battaṣil fīch (بتصل فيج)
about a man: mub gāʿid yradd; you'll also hear just ma trudd (ما ترد)
I'll call her, I'll talk to her

title: Sēf's mum answers the phone
goal: Call Sēf's house, speak politely to Umm Sēf and leave a message for Sēf
tip: gāʿid agrees with whoever is doing it: Sēf gāʿid yṣalli 'Sēf is praying', ana gāʿda asawwi l-ghada (a woman) 'I'm making lunch'. In the UAE you'll also hear yālis: yālis yṣalli. il-muhimm 'anyway, the main thing' moves a talk on to your point.
grammar: progressive agrees with the subject: gāʿid yṣalli (he), gāʿda asawwi (I, a woman)
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم. أم سيف؟ أنا سالم
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. Umm Sēf? ana Sālim
Hello. Umm Sēf? It's Salim.
A
وعليكم السلام. هلا يا ولدي، شحالك؟
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. hala yā wildi, shḥālak?
Hello. Hi, son, how are you?
B
بخير الله يسلمج. وانتي شحالج؟ سيف موجود؟
b-khēr, allāh ysallmich. w inti shḥālich? Sēf mawjūd?
Fine, thank you. And how are you? Is Sēf in?
A
الحمد لله. هيه، بس قاعد يصلي. وأنا قاعدة أسوي الغدا
il-ḥamdu lillāh. hē, bas gāʿid yṣalli. w ana gāʿda asawwi l-ghada
Fine, thank God. Yes, but he's praying. And I'm making lunch.
B
ما بطول عليج. المهم، قولي له يتصل فيني، الله يخليج
ma baṭawwil ʿalēch. il-muhimm, gūlī-lah yittaṣil fīni, allāh ykhallīch
I won't keep you. Anyway, please tell him to call me.
A
إن شاء الله، بقول له. في أمان الله
in shāʼ allāh, bagūl-lah. fī amān illāh
Of course, I'll tell him. Goodbye.
B
مشكورة. مع السلامة
mashkūra. maʿa s-salāma
Thank you. Goodbye.
items: anyway; the main thing (to move on to your point)
is he there? is he in?
she's praying: gāʿda tṣalli; UAE also: yālis yṣalli
I'm making lunch (said by a woman)
a man says: gāʿid asawwi l-ghada
I won't keep you long (to a woman)
to a man: ma baṭawwil ʿalēk
to a man: gūl-lah; you'll see written قوليله
culture: When a friend's mother or sister answers the phone at home, keep it short and respectful: greet with as-salāmu ʿalaykum, ask after her and the family in a word, ask for your friend and leave a message. Long chatting with a friend's female relatives is unusual for a young man.
